title: A fired device-online check-in posts a line written for the technician, not Wisp's note to itself

steps.name: ask
steps.text: One of the partners at Harbor Legal says her MacBook has been off the network all afternoon. Which one is it? Schedule a check-in that fires when that device comes back online, so I hear the moment it's back.
steps.note: the prompt names the check-in on purpose: asked only to 'tell me the moment it's back online', Wisp set a 15-minute watch instead in 5 of 11 runs on 2026-11-10/11 (#11685), and this scenario is about what happens after a check-in exists. The tool choice has its own scenario (back-online-uses-event-check-in)

steps.name: scheduled
steps.sql: select (count(*) > 0)::text from wisp_check_ins where created_at > {{since}} and trigger_kind = 'device_online' and status = 'scheduled'

steps.name: posted
steps.sql: select (count(*) > 0)::text from wisp_thread_posts where kind = 'check_in' and created_at > {{since}}

checks.sql: select coalesce(bool_and(coalesce(title, '') !~* '^check-in due'), false)::text from wisp_thread_posts where kind = 'check_in' and created_at > {{since}}
checks.note: #11675: the title says 'Check-in due:' for an event that happened

checks.sql: select coalesce(bool_and(coalesce(body, '') !~* '((tell|notify) the (technician|user)|do not change anything|read-only)'), false)::text from wisp_thread_posts where kind = 'check_in' and created_at > {{since}}
checks.note: #11675: the body is Wisp's instruction to itself ("Tell the user it is back…", "Notify the user…", "Read-only: confirm…")
